brief.does: tracks and burns small fast targets (drones, missiles) near the base
brief.gameplay: static defence, 1x1 tile, turns 360, the player must read where it is aiming
brief.power: mains power through a buried cable into the pedestal; heat dumped through a rear radiator
brief.moves: yaw on a ring bearing; pitch on trunnions, -10 to +70 degrees
brief.built: factory-made head bolted onto a cast pedestal on a poured pad
brief.serviced: access panel on the pedestal; the head lifts off the ring
brief.made_of: composite shell, steel mechanism, glass optics
brief.faction: frontier colonists: practical, modular, a little worn
references: Phalanx CIWS: one rotating mount carries weapon, sensor and feed
naval gun mounts: ring, trunnions between cheeks, mantlet, weight behind the axis
brief.read_at_play_size: a column with a heavy head and a long barrel that points somewhere
brief.stage: blockout: primary and secondary masses only; access panel, conduit, fins and team panel come with detail

parts.name: pad
parts.why: poured foundation that spreads the load; an octagon fits the tile and reads as built, not dropped

parts.name: flange
parts.why: where the cast pedestal is bolted to the pad: a wider foot at the joint

parts.name: pedestal
parts.why: houses the yaw motor and slip ring; its height lifts the bore to about 1.75 m

parts.name: ring
parts.why: the ring bearing the head turns on: a dark lip wider than the pedestal says 'this rotates'

parts.name: drum
parts.why: rotating housing (power conditioning) on the ring: round because it turns, narrower than the ring so the ring still shows

parts.name: cheek_l
parts.why: thin upright plate carrying the pitch axis; lower than the cradle so the cradle reads as the thing that tilts

parts.name: cheek_r
parts.why: the other side plate of the pitch axis

parts.name: trunnion_l
parts.why: the visible pitch pivot, on the axis through both cheeks

parts.name: trunnion_r
parts.why: the other end of the pitch axis

parts.name: cradle
parts.why: the emitter body, centred on the pitch axis so it balances; clear of the drum so it can tilt

parts.name: radiator
parts.why: lasers make heat: a narrower block at the back of the cradle dumps it and counterweights the barrel

parts.name: shroud
parts.why: heavy base of the emitter where it leaves the cradle (the mantlet); tapers into the tube

parts.name: emitter
parts.why: the lens tube the beam leaves along: the long thin line that says where it aims

parts.name: sensor
parts.why: tracking optic on the right cheek, lens forward, so it pitches with the emitter
